question.hi: Ek point circle ke andar hai, toh us point se kitni tangents nikalti hain?
question.en: How many tangents can be drawn from a point that lies inside a circle?

explanation.hi: Circle ke andar ke kisi point se koi tangent nahi nikalti — koi tangent possible nahi hai.
explanation.en: No tangent can be drawn from a point inside the circle.

question.hi: Tangent, point of contact pe radius ke sath kya angle banati hai?
question.en: What angle does a tangent make with the radius at the point of contact?

explanation.hi: Theorem 10.1 ke according, tangent hamesha radius ke perpendicular (90°) hoti hai.
explanation.en: By Theorem 10.1, a tangent is always perpendicular (90°) to the radius.

question.hi: Ek external point se ek circle pe kitni tangents draw ki ja sakti hain?
question.en: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from an external point?

explanation.hi: External point se hamesha exactly 2 tangents nikalti hain.
explanation.en: Exactly 2 tangents can always be drawn from an external point.

question.hi: PA aur PB ek circle pe external point P se do tangents hain. Agar PA = 9cm, to PB kya hoga?
question.en: PA and PB are two tangents drawn to a circle from an external point P. If PA = 9cm, what is PB?

explanation.hi: Theorem 10.2 ke according, external point se dono tangents ki length equal hoti hai — PB = PA = 9cm.
explanation.en: By Theorem 10.2, the two tangents from an external point are equal in length — PB = PA = 9cm.

question.hi: Quadrilateral OAPB mein (O centre, PA/PB tangents), ∠AOB + ∠APB ka sum kya hota hai?
question.en: In quadrilateral OAPB (O = centre, PA/PB tangents), what is the sum ∠AOB + ∠APB?

explanation.hi: ∠OAP aur ∠OBP dono 90° hote hain (tangent ⊥ radius), aur quadrilateral ke angles ka sum 360° hota hai, isliye baaki dono angles ka sum bhi 180° hi hoga.
explanation.en: Since ∠OAP and ∠OBP are both 90° (tangent ⊥ radius) and the quadrilateral's angles sum to 360°, the remaining two angles must also add up to 180°.

question.hi: Circle ka radius 6cm hai aur ek point centre se 10cm door hai. Tangent ki length kya hogi?
question.en: A circle has radius 6cm and a point is 10cm from the centre. What is the length of the tangent?

question.hi: Prove karo ki circle ke kisi bhi point pe tangent, us point of contact se guzarne wale radius ke perpendicular hoti hai.
question.en: Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

answer.hi:
Given: Circle with centre O, tangent XY at point P.
To Prove: OP ⊥ XY
Proof by Contradiction:
Maan lo OP ⊥ XY nahi hai.
Toh koi aur point Q hoga XY pe jisse OQ ⊥ XY ho.
Right triangle OQP mein, OQ < OP (hypotenuse sabse badi).
Lekin Q circle ke andar hai (kyunki OQ < radius OP), iska matlab XY circle ko do points pe kaat rahi hai — contradiction!
Isliye OP ⊥ XY hi hona chahiye.
answer.en:
Given: Circle with centre O, tangent XY at point P.
To Prove: OP ⊥ XY
Proof by Contradiction:
Assume OP is not perpendicular to XY.
Then there would be some other point Q on XY such that OQ ⊥ XY.
In right triangle OQP, OQ < OP (hypotenuse is the largest side).
But then Q lies inside the circle (since OQ < radius OP), which means XY cuts the circle at two points — a contradiction!
Therefore, OP must be perpendicular to XY.

question.hi: Prove karo ki ek external point se circle pe draw ki gayi do tangents ki lengths equal hoti hain.
question.en: Prove that the lengths of the two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal.

answer.hi:
Given: Circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PA and PB.
To Prove: PA = PB
Proof: Join OP, OA, OB.
∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Theorem 10.1)
OA = OB (radii of same circle)
OP = OP (common side)
ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP (RHS congruence rule)
Isliye, PA = PB (CPCT).
answer.en:
Given: Circle with centre O, external point P, tangents PA and PB.
To Prove: PA = PB
Proof: Join OP, OA, OB.
∠OAP = ∠OBP = 90° (Theorem 10.1)
OA = OB (radii of same circle)
OP = OP (common side)
ΔOAP ≅ ΔOBP (by RHS congruence rule)
Therefore, PA = PB (by CPCT).

question.hi: Ek circle ka radius 7cm hai. External point P se do tangents PA aur PB draw ki gayi hain. Agar ∠APB = 60°, toh (i) tangent ki length nikaalo, (ii) OP ki length nikaalo.
question.en: The radius of a circle is 7cm. Two tangents PA and PB are drawn from an external point P. If ∠APB = 60°, find (i) the length of the tangent, (ii) the length of OP.

answer.hi:
Given: OA = 7cm, ∠APB = 60°
Theorem 10.2 se PA = PB, isliye ΔPAB isosceles hai.
∠PAB = ∠PBA = (180°−60°)/2 = 60°
Quadrilateral OAPB mein ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180°, isliye ∠AOB = 120°
ΔOAP mein: ∠OAP = 90°, ∠AOP = 60° (OP, ∠AOB ko bisect karti hai)
tan 30° = OA/PA → PA = 7√3 cm
sin 30° = OA/OP → OP = 14cm
answer.en:
Given: OA = 7cm, ∠APB = 60°
By Theorem 10.2, PA = PB, so ΔPAB is isosceles.
∠PAB = ∠PBA = (180°−60°)/2 = 60°
In quadrilateral OAPB, ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180°, so ∠AOB = 120°
In ΔOAP: ∠OAP = 90°, ∠AOP = 60° (OP bisects ∠AOB)
tan 30° = OA/PA → PA = 7√3 cm
sin 30° = OA/OP → OP = 14cm

question.hi: Do concentric circles hain jinke radii 5cm aur 3cm hain. Bade circle ki ek chord chhote circle ko touch karti hai. Chord ki length nikaalo.
question.en: Two concentric circles have radii 5cm and 3cm. A chord of the larger circle touches the smaller circle. Find the length of the chord.

answer.hi:
Common centre = O. R = 5cm (bada), r = 3cm (chhota).
Chord AB chhote circle ko point P pe touch karti hai, isliye OP ⊥ AB aur OP = 3cm.
Right triangle OAP mein: OA² = OP² + AP² → 25 = 9 + AP² → AP = 4cm
Chord AB = 2 × AP = 8cm
answer.en:
Common centre = O. R = 5cm (larger), r = 3cm (smaller).
Chord AB touches the smaller circle at point P, so OP ⊥ AB and OP = 3cm.
In right triangle OAP: OA² = OP² + AP² → 25 = 9 + AP² → AP = 4cm
Chord AB = 2 × AP = 8cm

question.hi: Ek circle mein tangent XY point P pe chord PQ ko milti hai. Agar ∠XPQ = 70°, toh minor arc PQ ke centre pe banne wale angle ka value nikaalo.
question.en: A tangent XY meets chord PQ at point P on a circle. If ∠XPQ = 70°, find the angle subtended by the minor arc PQ at the centre.

answer.hi:
Alternate Segment Theorem se: ∠XPQ = Angle in alternate segment = 70°
Minor arc PQ pe centre angle = 2 × 70° = 140°
answer.en:
By the Alternate Segment Theorem: ∠XPQ = Angle in alternate segment = 70°
Angle subtended by minor arc PQ at the centre = 2 × 70° = 140°
